stem: Several family members develop headache, dizziness, nausea, and confusion after a portable generator was operated inside the home. Which exposure should the nurse suspect first?
rationale: CDC identifies portable generators used indoors as a major source of carbon monoxide exposure. Common symptoms include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea/vomiting, chest pain, and confusion. Multiple people with similar nonspecific symptoms plus a generator exposure strongly raises concern for carbon monoxide poisoning and requires urgent evaluation and removal from the source.
educational_objective: Recognize the exposure history and symptom pattern of carbon monoxide poisoning.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_claim_supported: Supports indoor generator exposure as a CO source and the associated headache, dizziness, nausea, and confusion symptom pattern.
correction_summary: Retained the strong exposure-recognition construct and removed competing diagnostic overreach.
audit_findings: A uniquely integrates the shared symptoms with the generator exposure.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14 / PDF p.18
